title: Onion Soup Gratinée
subtitle: Baked French onion soup with Gruyère croutons
excerpt: Deeply caramelised onions in a rich beef broth, ladled into oven-proof bowls, topped with a thick bread crouton soaked in broth, and blanketed with melted Gruyère. The definitive bowl of soup.

recipe.sourceNotes: Soupe à l'oignon gratinée is a Parisian classic, historically associated with the old central market of Les Halles and the working-class Parisian tradition of eating hearty soup at dawn after a night's work in the markets. The dish has been made in France in various forms since at least the seventeenth century but was elevated to a restaurant classic in the nineteenth century. The baked, cheesy version (gratinée) was made famous in its modern form by the Parisian restaurants of the 1800s. The caramelisation of the onions is the entire foundation of the dish: it must take at least 45 minutes and the onions must be deeply golden-brown, not merely softened. The Gruyère is the traditional cheese because it melts smoothly without becoming oily. This version is identical in method to the French-onion-soup recipe; the gratinée finish distinguishes this individual-bowl, oven-finished version.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy saucepan for the soup.

content.text: The onions must caramelise slowly over at least 45 minutes. The process has three stages: sweating (the onions soften and turn translucent), breaking down (they begin to collapse and release their liquid), and caramelising (the sugars concentrate and the onions turn deep amber). Most recipes underestimate how long this takes; rushing it with higher heat produces bitter, partially caramelised onions. Add a pinch of sugar if the onions seem reluctant to colour after 40 minutes.

Melt the butter and oil together in a large, heavy saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the onions, a pinch of salt, and the thyme. Cook for 45 to 55 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the onions are deep golden-brown and reduced by two-thirds.

Add the garlic and flour and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it bubble until absorbed. Add the stock and bay leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the thyme and bay.

Heat the grill to high. Ladle the soup into 4 oven-proof bowls on a baking tray. Float 2 toasted bread slices on each bowl. Pile the grated Gruyère thickly over the top. Place under the grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling, and beginning to brown. Serve immediately, warning that the bowls are very hot.
